# Module 6: Ecological Forecasting {#M6_1 -}

### Objectives {#M6_2 -}

To use an ecological forecasting model to predict lake primary productivity, and to work through the *iterative forecasting cycle* of building a model, forecasting with uncertainty, assessing the forecast against observations, and updating the model.

By the end of this module you should be able to:

- describe an ecological forecast and the iterative forecasting cycle
- explore and visualise ecological monitoring data
- calibrate a simple model of primary productivity and use it to generate a forecast **with uncertainty**
- adjust model parameters and inputs to see how they affect forecast performance
- compare forecasts between sites in different ecoclimatic regions

### Before you start {#M6_before_start -}

- Review the habitat and ecosystems lecture
- Think about forecasts you already rely on (weather, bushfire, algal bloom warnings) — what makes them useful, and how is their uncertainty communicated?

### Module Resources {#M6_3 -}

This week you'll be working through the **Macrosystems EDDIE** module [**Introduction to Ecological Forecasting**](https://macrosystemseddie.shinyapps.io/module5/), which runs in your browser — there is nothing to install.

The module uses data from the [National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON)](https://www.neonscience.org/) to forecast chlorophyll-*a* at a lake site of your choosing, driven by NOAA weather forecasts.

Start on the **Introduction** tab and **download the report template** — this is the worksheet you will complete as you go and submit at the end of the module.

```{block2, hintM6_1, type='rmdnote2'}
The app runs on a public server, so it can be slow at busy times and it will disconnect if you leave it idle. Fill in the report template and save the plots **as you go** rather than leaving it to the end of the class.
```

### Exercises {#M6_4 -}

Work through the three activities in order, answering the questions in the report template as you go.

#### Activity A: Visualise Data & Build Model {#M6_5 -}

1) Select a NEON lake site and read the site information.
2) Explore the variables measured at that site, and the relationships between them and chlorophyll-*a*.
3) Work through the nutrient–phytoplankton model, then **calibrate** it so that the simulated chlorophyll-*a* matches the observations.

#### Activity B: Generate & Assess Forecast {#M6_6 -}

4) Examine the NOAA weather forecast for your site and convert it into model inputs.
5) Generate a forecast of chlorophyll-*a* that includes uncertainty, and note which sources of uncertainty matter most.
6) Assess how well the forecast performed once observations become available.

#### Activity C: Complete the Forecast Cycle {#M6_7 -}

7) Update your model parameters using the new observations, and generate a second forecast.
8) Compare the two forecasts — did completing the cycle improve the forecast?

```{block2, hintM6_2, type='rmdtip2'}
A forecast without uncertainty is just a guess. When you write up your results, comment on the *width* of the forecast envelope as well as the position of the central line.
```
